fixtureDivergences.note: Render-conformance section: the shared conformance corpus (packages/adapter-tests) is rendered through every adapter’s REAL backend and byte-compared against the Hono reference. This answers, per fixture and per adapter, whether the construct WORKS — not just whether it compiles. A construct works either as written (✓) or with a documented `/* @client */` comment (✓†, a verified, supported escape — most refusals have one). Fixtures absent from the table below work on every adapter — most as written, some via that documented escape; the headline says how many of each. Listed fixtures need attention somewhere: a bare diagnostic code is still-open debt with no escape yet, a code led by ✗ owes no escape at all (by design), and ≠ means the fixture compiles clean but its rendered output diverges from the reference.

A '/* @client */' escape twin would SSR an empty region, eliminating the adopted DOM node the fixture exists to test patching — collapsing it to the already-covered client-only-loop case with zero new coverage. It is also deliberately kept out of integrations/shared/components (per this file's own docstring) because every DSL integration app's bf build compiles that directory wholesale, so no DSL escape variant is wanted there either.

ambient-locale-date-formatting.title: Ambient-locale Date formatting
ambient-locale-date-formatting.given: a `Date`-typed prop formatted with zero-argument `toLocaleDateString()` (no explicit locale or options)
ambient-locale-date-formatting.expected: the date renders formatted for the server process default locale
ambient-locale-date-formatting.actual: the compiler refuses with BF021 (by design)
ambient-locale-date-formatting.reason: The zero-argument form resolves against the runtime environment ambient locale (ICU/CLDR data, `LC_*`), which is not knowable at build time and differs across every backend language and between the server and the browser. Any lowering would be a silent SSR/CSR divergence; a Hono carve-out was tried and rejected because hydration re-evaluates the expression against a JSON-de-riched receiver. The literal-locale and named-timezone forms are lowered instead.

array-fill.title: Array.prototype.fill in a template expression
array-fill.given: a template expression calling `.fill(value)` on an array
array-fill.expected: the filled array renders in the server HTML

boolean-in-static-loop-item.title: Boolean field in a static loop item
boolean-in-static-loop-item.given: a static array `.map()` whose item objects carry a boolean field, read by a conditional or a boolean attribute
boolean-in-static-loop-item.expected: each row renders in the server HTML with the boolean applied per item

child-prop-mirror-attr-ssr.title: Mirrored child-prop attribute appears only after hydration
child-prop-mirror-attr-ssr.given: a non-standard named prop passed to a child component call (`<VariantTag variant={variant()} />`) that the compiler mirrors onto the child root as a DOM attribute
child-prop-mirror-attr-ssr.expected: the server HTML and the hydrated DOM carry the same attributes on the child root
child-prop-mirror-attr-ssr.actual: renders the child root without the attribute in the server HTML; the hydration effect then adds it, so pre- and post-hydration DOM differ

client-only-loop-in-static-loop.title: Client-only nested loop inside a static loop row
client-only-loop-in-static-loop.given: a static (non-signal) array `.map()` whose row contains a `/* @client */` nested `.map()`
client-only-loop-in-static-loop.expected: the outer rows render in the server HTML, each with an empty inner loop host for the client to fill

computed-const-loop-source.title: Computed component-scope const as a loop source
computed-const-loop-source.given: a `.map()` whose array is a component- or module-scope `const` computed from props or a function call
computed-const-loop-source.expected: the rows render in the server HTML

derived-object-literal-signal.title: Derived object-literal signal initializer
derived-object-literal-signal.given: a `createSignal` / `createMemo` whose initial value is an object literal referencing a live prop (with or without a spread)
derived-object-literal-signal.expected: field reads on the signal render the values the caller passed

fragment-wrapped-conditional-return-bran.title: Fragment-wrapped branch of a conditional return is never hydrated
fragment-wrapped-conditional-return-bran.given: a component with an early-return branch whose other branch is wrapped in a fragment (`if (x) return <a/>; return <><button/></>`)
fragment-wrapped-conditional-return-bran.expected: the rendered branch root carries the component scope id on every render path, so its events bind
fragment-wrapped-conditional-return-bran.actual: renders the fragment-wrapped branch root without a scope id after hydration (the server HTML is correct, a pure client mount is correct), so its events never bind

jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.title: JSX wrapped in a ternary or array at a non-children prop
jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.given: a component prop other than `children` whose value is a ternary or array literal wrapping JSX elements (`header={cond ? <a/> : <b/>}`)
jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.expected: the chosen elements render inside the child in the server HTML
jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.actual: the compiler refuses with BF021 (by design)
jsx-wrapped-in-non-children-prop.reason: The shape is refused in the shared JSX-to-IR phase, identically on every adapter including the reference: the classifier has no structured node for it, and the only alternative was splicing raw JSX source text into the emitted client JS untyped. Passing the elements as `children`, or lifting the ternary into a single JSX element, is the supported form.

loop-row-rest-bag-prop-override.title: Per-row prop routed into a child rest bag inside a composite loop row
loop-row-rest-bag-prop-override.given: a signal-driven `.map()` whose row root is a plain element wrapping a child component, passing a per-row value through a prop the child captures only via `...rest`
loop-row-rest-bag-prop-override.expected: each row renders the child with that row's value applied (`title="one"`, `title="two"`)
loop-row-rest-bag-prop-override.actual: renders the child without the rest-bag attribute at all, on every row

module-scope-helper-call.title: Module-scope helper called from a template position
module-scope-helper-call.given: a template expression calling a module-scope helper by bare name (an arrow-valued `const`, a `function` declaration, or a chain of them), in text or boolean-test position
module-scope-helper-call.expected: the helper runs at render time and its result renders in the server HTML
module-scope-helper-call.actual: the compiler refuses with BF101 / BF102

namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.title: Reactive primitive called through a namespace import
namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.given: a reactive primitive invoked through a namespace import (`import * as bf`, `bf.createSignal(...)`) in a compile with no shared `ts.Program`
namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.expected: the signal is declared and the component hydrates
namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.actual: the compiler refuses with BF013 (by design)
namespace-import-primitive-without-progr.reason: Without a type checker the analyzer fast path matches only a bare identifier callee, so the declaration would be silently dropped and every reference would throw at hydrate. The loud refusal is the permanent answer for checker-less compiles; a compile that supplies a shared program (the Vite plugin does) resolves the primitive normally and never reaches it. Importing the primitive by name is the supported form.

nested-callback-in-filter-predicate.title: Nested higher-order callback inside a filter predicate
nested-callback-in-filter-predicate.given: a `.filter()` predicate whose body calls `.some()` / `.find()` with its own arrow callback
nested-callback-in-filter-predicate.expected: the filtered rows render in the server HTML with the nested predicate applied

off-subset-callback-body.title: Off-subset expression in a collection-method callback
off-subset-callback-body.expected: the callback runs and the result renders in the server HTML
off-subset-callback-body.actual: the compiler refuses with BF021 / BF101

ref-effect-attr-state-ssr.title: Attribute state computed in a ref callback or mount effect never reaches SSR
ref-effect-attr-state-ssr.given: a component that writes a reactive attribute (`aria-expanded`, `aria-checked`, `data-selected`, `data-mounted`) as a compile-time JSX literal and computes its real value inside a `ref` callback or a mount effect (context reads, `createEffect`)
ref-effect-attr-state-ssr.expected: the server HTML and the hydrated DOM carry the same attribute value
ref-effect-attr-state-ssr.actual: renders the compile-time literal in the server HTML (a `ref` callback never runs at SSR) and the first client effect pass then writes the computed value, so pre- and post-hydration DOM differ — a visible snap at the hydrate boundary

rich-typed-prop-hydration.title: Rich-typed prop read by client code
rich-typed-prop-hydration.given: a prop typed as a JSON-unsafe host type (`Map`, `Set`, `WeakMap`, `WeakSet`, `URLSearchParams`, `RegExp`, `Promise`, `Error`, `Symbol`, `BigInt`, `Function`) that the component own client code reads
rich-typed-prop-hydration.expected: the client handler sees the same value the server rendered with
rich-typed-prop-hydration.actual: the compiler refuses with BF049 (by design)
rich-typed-prop-hydration.reason: Props cross the `bf-p` hydration boundary as `JSON.stringify` data with no type-aware revival, so these types lose their contents (`Map` / `Set` serialize to `{}`, `BigInt` throws, `Promise` / `Function` cannot cross a serialization boundary at all). A typed revival envelope was considered and rejected as a nine-adapter protocol change that still could not carry every listed type. The sound path is to pass a JSON-safe value and rebuild the rich value client-side.

select-out-of-range-selected-index.title: Out-of-range controlled select: placeholder selected on the server, nothing selected after hydration
select-out-of-range-selected-index.given: a controlled `<select value={...}>` with statically enumerable `<option>`s whose bound value matches none of them
select-out-of-range-selected-index.expected: the server-rendered select and the hydrated select agree on the live selection (`selectedIndex` / `value`)
select-out-of-range-selected-index.actual: renders the hidden placeholder option selected (`selectedIndex` 0, `value` ""); the hydration controlled-value effect then assigns the out-of-range value, which the browser resolves to no selection (`selectedIndex` -1), so the live state changes across hydration although both read as blank

signal-read-in-nested-static-loop.title: Signal read inside a nested static loop row
signal-read-in-nested-static-loop.given: a static (non-signal) array `.map()` whose row contains a nested `.map()` reading a signal or memo getter
signal-read-in-nested-static-loop.expected: both loop levels render in the server HTML with the signal initial value

statement-body-callback.title: Statement-carrying .map() / .flatMap() callback body

statement-body-callback.expected: the callback body runs and every row renders in the server HTML
